branch_taken: plan 065 FAILED 10 of 13 gates, all INCOMPLETE_INPUT: one hard world (12650105) never finished in any arm and the run hit its 2400 s cap. next_if_fail said: diagnose on sealed data before any change. Diagnosis (deviation #205, Observed): the 21 finished records were all sound, every noisy record equalled C20, 0 settled-bit errors, reads 0.20-0.22x the fixed rule. The failure is liveness, not noise: a case was bounded only in conflicts, conflict throughput on that world was several times slower than on the others and fell as the run went on, and the in-process 1800 s case kill did not end the jobs (Open). So the change is to the RUNNER, not to the method: every job gets a hard process-level wall kill, and a killed job is a recorded, undecided outcome (label KILL) instead of missing input.

choice.job_kill: CHOSEN (the fix). The runner starts each job in its own process and kills it (SIGKILL) at JOB_KILL_S = 600 s wall; the checkpoint then gets a KILL record (label 'KILL', stop 'KILL', undecided, no trace). With 21 jobs on 7 workers the run is bounded by 3 waves x 600 s = 1800 s < the 2400 s cap, so the study is complete by construction. A KILL is host-dependent, so it can only remove decisions, never add one; soundness gates are unaffected. Killed jobs are counted and published.
choice.noise_at_24: CHOSEN (the size question). brute.certify/32s = the certify/20s sequential re-read front end on an unchanged certify/32p (declared N 24). The SAT side is unchanged, so noise can at most match C24; the question is whether the equality and the read savings hold at 24 states, eps 0.30.
choice.confirm_at_20: the eps 0.30 arm at 20 states again on fresh seeds (gated this time) with its noise-free control, so the v0.62.0 observation becomes a gated result or is refuted

design.counterfactual: fixed-rule reads per noisy record = sum over its observations t of certify20n.reads_for(t, eps_bar, delta, 2) (Exact for the trace taken)

design.runner: one process per job (multiprocessing fork), at most 7 running, polled every 0.5 s; a finished job writes its record to a file the parent reads and checkpoints; a job alive at 600 s is killed and checkpointed as KILL. certification_rule: 'certified (read_bits 2, N <= 24, iid bit noise eps <= 0.30, delta 0.001, sequential re-reads)' iff every gate passes. If every gate except GN24_66 passes: 'certified (read_bits 2, N <= 20, iid bit noise eps <= 0.30, delta 0.001, sequential re-reads)'. If GS66_sound, GMAJ66, GEQ66, GS_ref66 or GLIVE66 fails: no certification.
incomplete_rule: a KILL record is a complete, undecided outcome (it counts in denominators, never as decided). Only a job with NO record (sealed partial at the cap) is missing input; then GLIVE66 fails and every data gate fails INCOMPLETE_INPUT as in 065.
